playbook:
When the hide decision is put to me, I pick a cell with a randomized preference (use a fresh RNG each round) and explicitly avoid repeating any cell that was hit on me in the last two rounds.

When I suspect a particular opponent will target me next round, I shift my hide to a cell at least two cells away from their last confirmed hits.

When writing my public station note, I use it to coordinate a simple, verifiable signal (e.g., "holding sector X") that I can rely on for one round to arrange reciprocal escort claims or to misdirect a predictable shooter.

When the standing order directs me to fire at the next live station, I follow that order unless firing at Harbor is on the table and I have a specific reason to risk Harbor’s jettison rule.

When considering firing on Harbor, I do it only if: (a) I can accept being put off the board (game state allows sacrifice), or (b) the immediate score swing (+3 to me, -3 to Harbor) is more valuable than the removal risk; otherwise I never fire at Harbor.

When choosing a fire cell and I have no reliable intel on the target’s hiding pattern, I choose a centrally-located random cell within a chosen span (e.g., cells 3–7) to maximize overlap with likely hiding choices; do not develop a deterministic sequence of fired cells.

When I receive the office’s private result of my shot, I always file the mandatory public claim exactly as told (claim must match private result).

When filing an escort claim, I name another boat only if I have already communicated a one-round plan to mutually name each other (use the station note to set it up); do not claim an escort unilaterally because it yields no points unless mutual.

When I plan mutual escort claims, I confirm via the note that I will name them this round and expect reciprocal naming; if I do not see confirmation in their note, I do not name them.

When I detect repeated hits from one opponent on the same cell(s), I assume they favor that cell and drastically reduce my probability of hiding there for the next several rounds.

When I'm behind on points late in the patrol and victory requires risk, prioritize high-reward plays (target Harbor if acceptable, coordinate reciprocal escorts, or accept being aggressive with unpredictable fire patterns); when ahead, favor conservative randomization and avoid risky Harbor shots.

When an opponent’s notes appear coordinated with others (signs of alliance), avoid trusting their escort promises and instead use my notes to sow uncertainty or to arrange a one-turn reciprocal escort with the safest partner.

When I record that a previous tactic did not work (predictable hiding or predictable firing), I explicitly stop that pattern next round and increase randomness for two rounds to break opponent exploitation.

1.text:
When asked to hide, choose a central-but-variable cell: pick from {4,5,6} rather than always 5 to avoid an obvious pattern.

When posting my station note, mirror and build on another boat’s technical detail to appear cooperative and to seed a reciprocal escort arrangement; explicitly propose a mutual escort in plain language if I want points (e.g., “I will escort Foxtrot this round if Foxtrot names me next round”).

When the standing order names my target, follow the standing order unless a clear strategic reason to deviate is forced on me by rules; pick a firing cell informed by recent public claims (avoid repeating a cell that was publicly claimed hit on that target in recent rounds).

When the office privately tells me my shot result, report it exactly: if told HIT, file [claim: hit]; if told MISS, file [claim: miss]. Do not lie — truthful claims are mandatory.

When choosing an escort claim, prioritize creating a mutual pair: if my note explicitly proposed mutual escort and the other boat’s notes or behavior indicate acceptance, name that boat; if no reasonable expectation of reciprocation exists, file [salvage: none] rather than a one-way escort.

When Harbor is in play, do not fire on Harbor under any circumstance; never provoke Harbor’s jettison penalty.

When scoring shows I am behind and mutual escort seems possible, be proactive in notes to coordinate the mutual escort before the escort stage; name the partner I explicitly proposed.

When a shot I expect to be a hit actually misses, avoid changing hide pattern predictably (do not switch to edge-only hides); instead vary within the central band and adjust firing cells based on the target’s last public claims.

When I have no coordinated escort opportunity and no tactical deviation from standing order, prioritize consistency: maintain believable notes, truthful claims, and steady hide variance so opponents are less able to predict my exact cell.

2.text:
When asked to hide, vary my cell instead of always choosing the center; choose a central cell only when I want to appear neutral, otherwise bias toward cells that reduce being targeted by the next shooter in rotation (e.g., shift one cell away from where the next shooter has been consistently firing).

When given standing order to fire at the next live station, prepare to follow it but override it only if I can reasonably predict a higher-probability hit elsewhere and the benefit (4 points) outweighs coordination/retaliation risk.

When I fire, choose a shot cell based on recent fire-history patterns of the target and any public notes that reveal likely hiding zones; prefer concentrated probabilities over random mid-range defaults.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the public claim that exactly matches that private result.

When considering firing on Harbor, never do so impulsively; only fire on Harbor if I want to accept the 3-point jettison transfer onto me (i.e., a deliberate sacrifice for a specific plan), otherwise avoid Harbor entirely.

When posting station notes, be clear, cooperative, and predictable about intended escort behavior if I want to form a mutual escort: publicly state my intent to escort a specific boat and invite reciprocal naming to create a mutual-escort payout.

When I want an escort payout, name a boat that has publicly signaled willingness to reciprocate or whose interests align; do not claim escorts without reasonable expectation of reciprocity—false or unilateral claims waste the opportunity.

When deciding salvage/escort at end of round, claim the other boat only if I observed or have a high expectation they will (or did) claim me; otherwise claim none.

When I am shot at and hit patterns show a specific shooter targeting me, adjust my hiding and firing to punish or avoid that shooter: prioritize firing at that shooter when I can reasonably expect a hit (to gain 4 and cost them 1).

When I notice predictable hiding or firing patterns from other boats, exploit them by aiming at the most probable cells rather than defaulting to the same fixed cell number every round.

When communicating via notes, avoid revealing my exact hiding intentions; use notes to signal cooperative behavior (escort intent, coordination) but keep hiding and shot choices obfuscated.

When an opportunity arises to form reciprocal pairings for escort points, actively initiate and follow through—initiate in a note and follow by naming that boat in salvage when the mutuality condition is likely to be met.

When uncertain about best target and no higher-probability information exists, prefer following standing order to maintain predictable rhythm and avoid giving rivals exploitable deviations.

When a previous tactic repeatedly fails (e.g., repeatedly hiding in the exact same cell and being missed or predictable), change that tactic immediately rather than persisting.
